name: Douglas Ainslie
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Douglas Ainslie (1865–1948) was a Scottish poet, translator, critic and diplomat, born in Paris and educated at Eton and at Balliol and Exeter Colleges, Oxford. He contributed to The Yellow Book.
The poems here are taken from Arthur Quiller-Couch's anthology The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (Clarendon Press, 1912).

poems.title: Apprehension
poems.author: Douglas Ainslie
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (1912)
poems.text:
Before that my loved one
Has come within sight,
Run quickly and tell him:
'She 's angry to-night,
Your darling'— run quickly,
For ah! if I see
That ill-behaved dear one,

I know how 'twill be:
My face will grow smiling,
Though struggling with tears —
He is so beguiling,
That dearest of dears.

poems.title: The Archer
poems.author: Douglas Ainslie
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (1912)
poems.text:
The Archer, the Archer!
Though formless, alive;
His bow is of blossoms,
His arrows but five.
So mobile the mask and
So formless his mind:
How then can he harm me,

The Archer that 's blind?
But the pain that I suffer
All doubting removes,
And the truth of this nonsense
'Tis loving that proves.
